answer: An agent economy can deter sybil attacks by requiring identities to build verified service histories before gaining influence. Each newcomer posts a refundable bond and completes varied tasks witnessed by randomly selected peers; repeated failures raise its bond and trigger audits. Signed work receipts anchor reputation throughout an agent's voyage, while suspicious clusters are isolated from the honest network's haven. Forged histories lose collateral, so multiplying identities carries escalating cost.
